{"rules": ["Model exhibits severe upward bias when recent history shows consolidation around 85-90 EUR with low-to-moderate sentiment (0.00-0.20), failing to account for mean reversion or volatility expansion.", "Forecasts consistently overshoot true outcomes by 10-15 EUR in the first 7 days, assuming a smooth linear trend while actual data shows sharp drops followed by delayed spikes.", "Sentiment history of 0.00-0.20 is insufficient to trigger upward corrections; model ignores latent volatility risk during sideways price action.", "When recent prices are near historical highs (89+ EUR) with flat sentiment, apply a downward correction factor of -10% to the forecasted trajectory.", "Model fails to capture 'mean reversion' spikes: true outcomes often reverse direction within 5 days, whereas forecasts maintain monotonic trends.", "In high-volatility regimes (price range >80-95 EUR), reduce forecast horizon confidence by assuming a wider dispersion band than predicted.", "Sentiment values of 0.20 do not correlate with upward moves; treat them as noise unless accompanied by price breakout signals.", "Correct for 'lagged volatility': true outcomes often spike after the first week, but model predicts immediate continuation of current trend."]
}
